evidence.observation: Public goal is repair of the existing Python sessionizer at /app/sessions: event-time sessions, journal restart, CLI flags, catalog last_run/ops-report, warehouse left intact. Binding contract and oncall notes are named.

Contract fully specifies tie-break vs feed order, fail-closed rejects, catalog session_gap overlay, half-open sessions, compare-then-update watermark, late-but-allowed vs TOO_LATE, journal seq/append/non-decreasing watermark, --reset-output not clearing journal, unknown flags exit 2 before journal/output touch, and empty-input no watermark advance.

Operator symptoms match the contract: 85000 classified on-time after a 100000 anchor, 1000ms straggler missing from late.jsonl, two tenants sharing u1 merged, --reset-output wiping watermark.journal, journal seq stuck at 1.
Captured run shows journal rewrite seq=1, watermark stepping backward after event_time_ms=1000, --reset-output clearing the journal, and unknown --replay-from still creating data/watermark.journal.
_touch_runtime() and --reset-output journal wipe run before argparse; unknown flags therefore mutate the journal. use_arrival_gap=True is hardcoded into process_events.
session_key discards tenant_id and returns ('*', user_id), so SessionStore/SessionKeyedState merge distinct tenants that share a user id.
Each event calls track.record() and updates state.max_observed before classify_lateness, violating compare-against-current-watermark-then-advance.
WatermarkTrack.record assigns max_observed_event_time_ms to the current event time instead of max(), so a later earlier event rewinds the watermark; observe() exists but is unused here.
append_journal write_text-replaces the whole journal with a single seq=1 line, matching the bounce log and the contract's append/seq/non-decreasing requirements failing together.
When use_arrival_gap is true, gap close uses arrival_index*1000 rather than event_time_ms, so --feed out-of-order event times cannot drive session membership.

Catalog overlay looks contract-faithful: enterprise session_gap_ms=45000, other catalog plans and non-catalog tenants keep processor.json; lateness/duration always from processor.json. Easy to over-read as a second product.

Successful runs rewrite last_run.json and ops-report.json from the warehouse catalog; record_processor_run can INSERT into warehouse catalog.sqlite, which a contract-first agent may treat as forbidden warehouse mutation.
ROOT is hardcoded to /app/sessions. Harbor layout matches; a local Windows diagnostic cannot drive the public CLI without that mount.
catalog.sqlite is generated at image build via tools/generate_seed.py and is not present in the shipped warehouse/ tree; CLI catalog_ready() fails closed without it.
No disposable Harbor/oracle run was available in this isolated diagnostic. EXECUTION must be SIMULATION_NOT_EXECUTED and FINAL_VERIFIER_RESULT must be NOT_RUN; no pytest/Harbor score was invented.

role_output.DIAGNOSTIC_SUMMARY: Simulated Claude/Claude-Code diagnostic evidence only, not official Claude Opus 4.8 (or GPT-5.5) trial evidence. Harbor/oracle was not run. A contract-first pass over instruction, session-contract, oncall, bounce log, then CLI/pipeline/store/journal reconstructs a repairable event-time sessionizer with several interacting starter defects. Official difficulty is predicted USEFUL: the spec is unusually complete, but watermark order, max-observed rewind, journal rewrite, tenant-key collapse, arrival-gap, and CLI pre-parse mutation must all be repaired together; the large catalog/ops surface invites over-scope.
role_output.FIRST_DIAGNOSIS: Not a greenfield rewrite. The public processor already has the right modules and schemas; production-looking paths are wrong in coupled ways that match the bounce: (1) session identity drops tenant, (2) watermark is updated before lateness and is assigned rather than maxed, (3) the journal is rewritten at seq=1, (4) --reset-output and unknown flags mutate the journal before argparse, (5) process_events is wired to arrival-index gap instead of event time.

role_output.FIRST_MEANINGFUL_DIVERGENCE: After mapping oncall/log symptoms to session_key, journal write_text(seq=1), and --reset-output, a Claude-style solver diverges from a three-line patch by going back to the watermark advance-order section. That reconstruction is the first place the starter still looks 'explained' by the log (85000 on_time, 1000 on_time, watermark_ms=-9000) but is actually two independent bugs (record-before-classify and assign-instead-of-max). Stopping at identity+journal+CLI leaves --feed lateness and restart still wrong.
LIKELY_REASONING_WALLS: Watermark: classify against pre-event W, then max-observed, then raw journal watermark (may be negative), then watermark-triggered closes using comparison W=max(0, raw).
WatermarkTrack.record replacing max_observed instead of observe()/max, which rewinds journaled watermark_ms.
Journal protocol: append one JSON line per parsed observation, monotonic seq from 1, never rewrite, never decrease watermark_ms across restarts.
CLI: validate --input/--feed/--empty-check and reject unknown flags with exit 2 before creating or truncating watermark.journal; --reset-output truncates side JSONL only.
use_arrival_gap=True / arrival_index*1000 silently ignoring event-time gaps on --feed.
session_key ('*', user_id) plus IdleClosePlanner pop_key (tenant_id, user_id) leaving closed sessions in the store.
Catalog enterprise session_gap overlay vs lab tenants that are absent from catalog.sqlite.
Empty-check ensure_empty creating files but not truncating leftover sessions.jsonl/late.jsonl.
Scope trap: ~90 environment modules (catalog rollups, reconcile plane, timers, diagnostics) that look load-bearing but are mostly operator desk around a small core.
Idempotent SHA-256 of sessions.jsonl/late.jsonl requiring stable JSONL serialization and deterministic close order, not just semantic equality.
role_output.ENVIRONMENT_TOOL_FRICTION: Public CLI and paths.py assume /app/sessions inside the digest-pinned Python image; catalog.sqlite is baked by generate_seed.py at Docker build and is not in the git warehouse/ tree. This Windows diagnostic could inspect sources but could not honestly drive Harbor or the in-container verifier. Friction is layout/bootstrap, not missing language tooling. tmux/asciinema are present in the agent image and are not part of the scored repair.
